items.prose: Superheated 1,460°C grey iron wash severely eroded the 45% alumina firebrick lining in the melt zone. Slag analysis showed 48% silica content, thinning the furnace shell to glowing red steel within twelve hours of continuous blast.

Premature slag deoxidation in the arc furnace caused phosphorus pentoxide to revert from the slag blanket back into the molten steel bath (0.08% P). Cast lathe chucks broke under initial impact due to extreme cold-shortness.

Excess fluorspar flux added to fluidize dross chemically attacked the refractory clay taphole cone. The plug dissolved catastrophically mid-heat, spilling four hundred kilograms of molten bronze across the sand casting floor.

Melting scavenged diesel engine crankshafts introduced 0.6% titanium, forming high-melting-point perovskite and titanium carbonitride scum that resisted normal fluxing. The viscous crust fouled the crucible lip and produced inclusions in cast crankshafts.

Submerging a plunging bell of pure scrap magnesium alloy into the 1,410°C iron ladle produced an explosive violent magnesium vapor boiling flare. Blinding white 2,800K light illuminated the foundry bay and scorched overhead crane hoist ropes.

High sulfur content (0.18%) in scavenged scrap steel combined with a lack of ferromanganese caused the Mn:S ratio to drop to 1.2:1. Cast machine bed ways developed glass-hard white cementite chill corners that stripped milling cutters.

Anthracite coal fines with 22% silica ash shifted slag basicity down to an acidic 0.72. The aggressive acidic slag dissolved the protective lime coating and burned through the water-cooled copper blast tuyere, blowing steam into the bosh.

Molten cupola slag stream tapped directly across a high-pressure 120 PSI steam nozzle spun forty tons of golden-grey vitreous mineral wool. The fibrous batting was bagged and used to thermally insulate steam heating mains and bakery ovens.
